title: What happened in AI — Aug 9, 2026
intro: China's AI labs made the day's loudest moves on pricing and benchmarks: Moonshot's roughly 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi model became the first Chinese-built system to top a major coding benchmark, DeepSeek is reportedly preparing a "significant" price hike, and model distillation is emerging as the next US-China competitive front — all signs the market is shifting from price-cutting toward scale and pricing power.

Beneath that, the coding-agent field kept crowding, with Meta launching its first entrant to challenge Claude Code and Codex, and Stripe published how it pairs graph search with state machines to automate database incident recovery in production.
highlights: Moonshot's roughly 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi model becomes the first Chinese-built system to top a major coding benchmark.
DeepSeek is reportedly planning a "significant" price hike, a sign China's AI API price war may be cooling.
Meta launches Muse Code, its first AI coding agent, aiming directly at Claude Code and Codex.
Stripe automates database incident recovery by modeling its infrastructure as a graph and pairing graph search with state machines.
Model distillation is emerging as the next US-China AI competitive front as compute costs and export controls bite.
A reported breach tied to a Chinese open-source AI project raises fresh supply-chain security concerns.

categories.name: New Coding Agents Crowd the Field
categories.summary: Meta entered the coding-agent race head-to-head with Claude Code and Codex, while smaller open-source projects kept lowering the bar for installable, task-specific agent skills.

articles.title: Meta Launches Muse Code, Its First AI Coding Agent to Take on Claude and Codex - Memeburn
articles.summary: Meta launched Muse Code, its first AI coding agent, positioning it as a direct challenger to Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex.

articles.title: I vibe coded with Qwen 3.6 on a platform it had never seen, and the model was never the bottleneck - XDA
articles.summary: One developer's account of vibe-coding with Qwen 3.6 on an unfamiliar platform found the model, not the surrounding tooling, was never the limiting factor.

articles.title: Agentcn – Installable AI Agents
articles.summary: AgentCN is a new open-source library of installable, customizable AI agents with one-command installation, letting developers own and modify the agent code directly.

articles.title: Show HN: Job Seeker – AI agent skills for job searching
articles.summary: Job Seeker packages markdown-based agent skills that coding agents like Devin, Claude, Cursor, and OpenCode can consume to automate job search end to end: searching LinkedIn, filling Easy Apply, tracking applications in a kanban board, and drafting replies.

categories.name: Production Reliability: Graphs Replace Runbooks
categories.summary: Stripe automated database incident recovery by modeling its infrastructure as a graph and pairing graph-search algorithms with state machines — a concrete example of agentic patterns landing in core ops, not just chat interfaces.

articles.title: Stripe Uses Graph Search and State Machines to Automate Database Remediation
articles.summary: Stripe's engineering team modeled its global infrastructure as a graph and combined graph-search algorithms with state machines to automate database incident recovery.

categories.name: China's Model Race Shifts From Price Wars to Scale
categories.summary: Moonshot's Kimi became the first Chinese-built model to top a major coding benchmark while DeepSeek and other Chinese firms move toward higher prices and larger models — a reversal of the price-cutting that defined the past year. Model distillation is emerging as the next front in that same US-China competition.

articles.title: Moonshot AI's 2.8 Trillion Parameter Model Just Became the First From China to Top a Major Coding Benchmark - The Motley Fool
articles.summary: Moonshot AI's roughly 2.8-trillion-parameter model became the first Chinese-built system to top a major coding benchmark, per The Motley Fool.

articles.title: Chinese AI Firms Pursue Larger Models, Higher Prices - 조선일보
articles.summary: Chinese AI firms are moving toward larger models and higher prices, a shift away from the aggressive undercutting that defined the past year of competition.

articles.title: DeepSeek to get a 'significant' price hike soon - mashable.com
articles.summary: DeepSeek is preparing a "significant" price increase, according to a report — one of the clearest signs yet that China's AI API price war is cooling.

articles.title: AI Model Distillation Becomes the New Battleground Between the US and China - Startup Fortune
articles.summary: Model distillation — compressing large models into smaller, cheaper ones — is emerging as the next US-China AI competitive front as compute costs and export controls bite.

categories.name: Security and Supply-Chain Risk in Open-Source AI

articles.title: Chinese Open-Source AI Breach Sparks Hacking Fears - chosun.com
articles.summary: A reported security breach tied to a Chinese open-source AI project is stoking fresh concern about the security posture of freely available open-weight tooling.

articles.title: Lessons from the hacks

categories.name: Publishers Start Serving Ads to AI Agents
categories.summary: Time has begun serving ads specifically to AI agents crawling its site — an early signal that publishers are starting to treat agentic traffic as a distinct, monetizable audience.

articles.title: Time has started serving ads to AI agents
articles.summary: Time has begun serving ads specifically to AI agents that crawl its site, treating agentic traffic as a distinct audience rather than blocking or ignoring it.
